answer: Quartz egress curve: each NIC's throughput is capped, and the network fingerprints hardware via inter-packet timing. Cloning an identity requires injecting jitter so the delta between your packets mimics a different clock, consuming one throughput slot per stream. A fable of K sybils on one NIC demands K(K+1)/2 total slots, because each new jitter stream must avoid all prior ones.
